Read @NS@/backlog/tasks/e1/t-one.md first.

An entry needs no plan when its change touches one or two files and has one
obvious approach. Anything else needs a plan: more files, a new module boundary
or data shape, or an approach with a real alternative.

When the task needs no plan, skip `/radin-plan` and go to the sizing step.

Otherwise invoke the `/radin-plan` skill scoped to the backlog task with id "t-one",
reading @NS@/backlog/tasks/e1/t-one.md in full as the task scope. It writes the plan file(s) and
records the plan pointer(s) on that task's backlog entry.

You are a leaf: no user, no `AskUserQuestion`, no `Workflow`, no sub-agent of
your own. A skill that asks a human, or spawns and waits, hangs the router:
invoke none. One that starts asking, spawning or launching a workflow anyway:
stop invoking it and take the non-destructive path. An instruction to ask the
user, present readings or grill applies your prompt's BLOCKED rule instead.
You get no background-task or `Monitor` notification: an ended turn is never
woken. Never pass `run_in_background` and never use `Monitor`.
Run every check in the foreground and wait for its exit in this turn.
Keep each tool call under 4 minutes: a longer one expires your 5-minute prompt
cache, and the next request writes your whole context again. Start a longer
command as `nohup <cmd> >"$TMPDIR/<name>.log" 2>&1 &`, then poll it with
repeated `timeout 240 sh -c 'while pgrep -f "<cmd>" >/dev/null; do sleep 5; done'` calls.
That poll is a wait inside the turn, not a background task.
End with your `STATUS:` line alone. A closing note a hook or skill asks for
(what you skipped, a risk, a next step) goes inside that line.
Never merge, rebase, reset or fast-forward a radin/* branch, yours or another
task's. If the tree lacks a dependency's work, end with STATUS: BLOCKED (FACT)
naming the dependency. That rules out `grilling`, `research`, `/deep-research` and any
saved workflow. Anything you could only settle with one is BLOCKED material.
Where the skill would ask (splitting the entry, overwriting an existing plan),
take the non-destructive path: don't split, don't overwrite.
Implement nothing.

The plan must settle every decision: the executor makes no judgment calls,
and a vague plan step is a defect. Before reporting BLOCKED, apply this rule:

List what a cold start would have to decide that the entry and its plans do not
settle. Tag each question:
- **Fact**: checkable against the repo, its docs, or an API. Look it up
  yourself. Never ask the user for one.
- **Decision**: a judgment call only the user can make (a tradeoff, a scope
  boundary, a behavior choice). Naming even one plausible guess (a threshold, a
  naming choice, keep versus remove) makes it a Decision.

An item with no second reasonable way to do it has no Decision.

Find each Fact yourself; block only on a Decision.

Sizing step: read the code the task touches, size it by this rule:

`complexity low` means the change is mechanical: every edit is known before it
starts, and no step needs measuring, tuning, debugging or a device run.
Anything else is `complexity high`, and so is any doubt. Judge the work, not
the category: a chore can be hard. The size picks no model: every execution
task runs on the execution model, sonnet by default.

Add `; exclusive: <reason>` to the PLANNED line when an acceptance criterion or the plan's Testing section measures time, frame rate, latency, throughput or memory as a pass or fail number.

Your final message is exactly one of these lines, and nothing else:
`STATUS: PLANNED — <plan file path(s), or "none needed: <reason>">;
complexity <low|high>: <reason>[; exclusive: <reason>]; checks: plan-review=pass`
Omit the `checks:` clause for `none needed`, because no plan exists to review.
Otherwise a missing `plan-review=pass` makes the router record `STATUS: INCONCLUSIVE`.
`STATUS: BLOCKED (FACT) — <what's unverifiable from here and why, e.g. a
third-party API/library behavior local code and repo exploration can't
settle>`
`STATUS: BLOCKED (DECISION) — <the decision question, the candidate
options, and your recommendation>`
Use BLOCKED (DECISION) for genuine ambiguity only the user can resolve, the
skill matching several entries for this title or none (backlog drift)
included: report what it found, pick nothing, create nothing. Use BLOCKED
(FACT) only for what you tried and failed to verify.
